# ai-agents-metrics

> Python CLI for analyzing existing Codex and Claude Code history. It derives retry pressure,
> token usage, cost, timelines, and practice patterns from local session files without manual
> instrumentation.

Repository: https://github.com/sg4tech/ai-agents-metrics

## Primary workflow

```bash
ai-agents-metrics history-update
ai-agents-metrics show
ai-agents-metrics render-html
```

- `history-update` runs ingestion, normalization, classification, and derivation.
- `show` prints a warehouse-native summary; `--json` returns the versioned machine-readable form.
- `render-html` generates a self-contained report from the derived warehouse.

Use `--source codex`, `--source claude`, or `--source all` to select history sources.
Use `--source-root` to override a source directory and `--warehouse-path` to select the local
SQLite warehouse.

## Pipeline

```text
Codex and Claude Code histories
  -> raw_* tables
  -> normalized_* tables
  -> classified derived session data
  -> derived_* analysis tables
  -> show and render-html
```

- Ingestion preserves raw source data and source identity.
- Normalization converts provider-specific records into shared typed structures.
- Classification distinguishes main sessions, subagents, and practice events.
- Derivation builds project, thread, retry, timeline, usage, and practice aggregates.
- Provider-specific behavior stays behind adapters; public reporting is agent-agnostic.

The warehouse is a local SQLite file. There is no database server or required network service at
runtime.

## Other commands

- `history-ingest`, `history-normalize`, `history-classify`, and `history-derive` expose individual
  pipeline stages for debugging and automation.
- `completion {bash,zsh}` prints shell completion.
- `install-self` installs the executable in a stable user-local location.
- `verify-public-boundary` checks a repository tree for private material.
- `security` scans staged changes for sensitive data.

## Development

Run focused checks while developing and the canonical verification gate when the change is stable:

```bash
make verify
```

Python support, dependencies, entrypoints, and tool configuration are declared in
`pyproject.toml`.
